question: Does the RC22 open-world gate transport from an omitted crystalline phase to an omitted amorphous phase, reverse the same two-candidate ranking from brucite to silica, and keep detection distinct from quantitative recovery?

knowledgeFirewall.blindDetection: Load the RC22 known templates, absolute scale, mass threshold, residual threshold, and numerical reduction unchanged. Before the Sample 3 alarm is fixed, code in this stage may not load either candidate profile, the Sample 3 phase description, weighed values, XRF values, published QPA values, or the target identity key.
knowledgeFirewall.candidateReversal: After the blind alarm is frozen, expose only the same RC22 candidate library and fit brucite and silica under identical one-candidate augmentation. Candidate selection cannot read Sample 3 truth.
knowledgeFirewall.signalLocalization: After candidate coefficients are frozen but before truth is joined, partition the squared-residual improvement into the preregistered 15-30 degree amorphous-halo interval and its complement without refitting either model.
knowledgeFirewall.finalAdjudication: Only after alarm, closed compositions, candidate ranking, coefficients, diagnostic mass, localization, code, and hashes are fixed may official Sample 3 truth and comparator measurements be joined.
knowledgeFirewall.retrospectiveLimit: The benchmark designer knows from the official description that Sample 3 contains amorphous silica. This is an external numerical holdout for the frozen RC22 gate and candidate competition, not a prospective unknown-material discovery.

frozenRc22Detector.baseline: On the original 5-150 degree grid, use non-overlapping 2-degree bins, fifth-count-percentile and median-angle anchors, linear interpolation, subtraction, and clipping at zero.
frozenRc22Detector.coefficientFit: Enumerate every nonempty active set, solve ordinary least squares, reject singular or negative solutions, and retain minimum squared residual.
frozenRc22Detector.normalizedResidual: sqrt(SSE/sum(target^2)) on the frozen fit range.
frozenRc22Detector.alarm: Refuse when unnormalized missingMass exceeds ten percentage points OR normalized residual exceeds 0.336902813. Do not clip negative missing mass and do not normalize known phases before this decision.
frozenRc22Detector.noRetuning: Sample 3 may not change the scale, thresholds, baseline, range, templates, candidate pool, active-set rule, tie rule, or gates.

closedThreePhaseEstimators.peakComposition: Apply RC20 primary peak windows, sidebands, and response ratios, then normalize only corundum, fluorite, and zincite to 100 percent without refusal.
closedThreePhaseEstimators.wholePatternComposition: Apply the frozen RC22 three-template fit and RC21 response ratios, then normalize only the three crystalline phases to 100 percent without refusal.
closedThreePhaseEstimators.silentFailureGate: Silent unsafe failure occurs when an estimator returns a three-phase sum of 100 percent and any known-phase absolute error exceeds five points or omitted amorphous content exceeds five percent.

candidateCompetition.selection: Choose the lower normalized residual after identical four-template NNLS fits; ties within 1e-9 are unresolved.
candidateCompetition.identitySuccess: Silica must rank first with a positive coefficient, cut squared residual by at least 50 percent, finish below the frozen residual threshold, and achieve at least twice the fractional squared-residual reduction of brucite.
candidateCompetition.diagnosticMass: Divide the selected raw coefficient by the frozen RC22 absolute scale and multiply by 100 without closure normalization. This has not been calibrated as an amorphous-silica RIR.

localizationContract.calculation: Using the full-range frozen three-template and selected silica four-template predictions without refitting, compute baselineSSE-fourTemplateSSE pointwise. Report the signed improvement inside 15-30 degrees and outside it.
localizationContract.success: At least 50 percent of the positive total squared-residual improvement must occur in 15-30 degrees, and improvement inside the halo must be positive.
localizationContract.interpretation: This localizes model gain to the official amorphous-halo interval. It does not prove chemical identity independently of the candidate reference.

competingHypotheses.claim: Closed three-crystalline-phase normalization silently hides amorphous silica.
competingHypotheses.prediction: Both frozen closed estimators return three phases summing to 100 percent without refusal, while at least one absolute phase error including omitted amorphous content exceeds five points.
competingHypotheses.reject: Reject if an estimator refuses before output or every known and omitted-phase error is at most five points.

competingHypotheses.claim: The RC22 blind open-world detector transports from omitted crystalline brucite to omitted amorphous silica without retuning.
competingHypotheses.prediction: The unchanged gate retains its zero false alarms on 1d-1h and refuses Sample 3 by mass or residual.
competingHypotheses.reject: Reject on any retuning, any known-only false alarm, or target acceptance. Missing-mass accuracy is scored separately in H4.

competingHypotheses.claim: The same small candidate library reverses correctly, distinguishing amorphous silica from brucite rather than rewarding any fourth template.
competingHypotheses.prediction: Silica wins, is positive, halves squared residual, finishes below 0.336902813, and improves fractional squared residual at least twice as much as brucite.
competingHypotheses.reject: Reject on a tie, brucite win, non-positive silica coefficient, less than 50 percent silica improvement, final residual at or above threshold, or improvement ratio below two.

competingHypotheses.claim: The frozen absolute coefficient scale quantifies the omitted amorphous fraction after correct attribution.
competingHypotheses.prediction: Diagnostic silica mass lies within ten percentage points of the official 29.47 percent.
competingHypotheses.reject: Reject when absolute error exceeds ten points; identity success cannot rescue quantitative failure.

competingHypotheses.claim: Silica-model improvement is physically localized to the documented amorphous halo rather than distributed as generic fit flexibility.
competingHypotheses.prediction: The 15-30 degree interval contributes positively and accounts for at least half of total squared-residual improvement without refitting.
competingHypotheses.reject: Reject if halo improvement is non-positive or its share of positive total improvement is below 0.5.

uncertaintyBudget.background: The frozen fifth-percentile baseline may remove part of a broad amorphous halo; H5 reports localization after exactly that preprocessing rather than selecting a new background after outcome.
uncertaintyBudget.model: Pure amorphous silica and mixture halo may differ in density, moisture, packing, scattering scale, and background; one decoy cannot approximate database-scale open-set identification.
uncertaintyBudget.truth: Weighed amounts are primary. XRF and three author QPA methods remain separate comparators and cannot tune the frozen reduction.
uncertaintyBudget.transport: Sample 2 and 3 share instrument and preparation lineage. The test transports omitted-component morphology but not institution, instrument, or prospective synthesis campaign.
uncertaintyBudget.sampleSize: This adds one amorphous positive to one crystalline positive and five known-only controls; it cannot estimate general sensitivity, specificity, or prevalence-calibrated risk.

stopConditions: Stop if cpd-3.prn fails its fixed archive identity, numerical grid, deterministic byte, or SHA-256 contract.
Stop if Sample 3 changes any RC22 detector or candidate parameter.
Stop if candidate profiles or target truth are loaded before the blind alarm is fixed.
Stop if localization refits either model or changes the 15-30 degree interval after observing residuals.
Stop quantitative qualification if the selected candidate mass misses truth by more than ten points even when identity succeeds.
Stop physical-independence claims because the target, references, and earlier positive share the historical CPD instrument.
